sources.entry: OpenBao | Community-driven fork of Vault for managing secrets

summary.one_liner: OpenBao is a community-driven, open-source fork of HashiCorp Vault for managing, storing, and distributing secrets, certificates, and keys.
summary.what_it_does: OpenBao stores arbitrary key/value secrets and encrypts them before writing to persistent storage, with the README naming disk and PostgreSQL as backends. It can generate dynamic secrets on demand for systems such as AWS or SQL databases and automatically revoke them when their lease expires. It offers encryption and decryption as a service so applications can encrypt data without storing it themselves. All secrets carry leases that clients can renew through built-in APIs, and revocation can target single secrets or trees of secrets, such as all secrets read by a given user. The repository also contains the website, documentation, and web UI source under the website and ui subtrees, and publishes the api/v2 and sdk/v2 Go libraries.
use_cases: store database credentials and API keys securely
generate short-lived AWS or SQL database credentials on demand
encrypt data before saving it to a database without writing custom crypto
rotate keys and revoke secrets after an intrusion
notable: Community-driven fork of HashiCorp Vault under open governance
Dynamic secrets with automatic revocation on lease expiry
Encryption and decryption without storing the data
Revocation of individual secrets or whole trees of secrets
Publishes importable api/v2 and sdk/v2 Go libraries
caveats: The README says importing the main openbao module into other projects is not a supported use
Development setup requires Go; the pinned toolchain is in .go-version
Security issues should be reported privately by email rather than public issues
